blocks.content: Despite being a small state (10,486 sq km), Tripura has a varied terrain. The state is divided into broad physiographic zones running in roughly north-south parallel ridges and valleys — a pattern determined by the Tripura folds (a series of folded anticlines and synclines).

cells: Flat alluvial plains bordering Bangladesh; densest population; Agartala; paddy cultivation; most urban development; elevation 15–30 m
Parallel ridges and valleys (jampui, shakhan, longtarai, atharamura ranges); elevation 200–900 m; rubber and tea cultivation; tribal settlements
Higher hills; Jampui Hills (highest range in Tripura); tea gardens; North Tripura district
Borders Mizoram; dense forest; tribal areas; Dhalai district
Beautiful hill range; orange orchards; tribal (Mizo/Reang/Lushai) settlements; Orange Festival held here; panoramic views; 'Switzerland of Tripura'
Dense forest; wildlife sanctuary corridor; Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary

blocks.content: The terrain of Tripura is characterised by the 'Tripura Folds' — a series of anticlinal (arched upward) and synclinal (curved downward) structures running roughly north-south, parallel to each other. These are remnants of Himalayan folding processes but are much older and more eroded. The anticlines form the ridges and the synclines form the valleys where rivers flow.

items: The anticlines (ridges) and synclines (valleys) are roughly parallel — creating the characteristic banded landscape of Tripura
Natural gas is found in the synclinal structures — the Tripura folds are the reason Tripura has significant natural gas reserves
Oil and gas explorers use this geological structure to locate gas deposits
The terrain makes construction of roads and infrastructure challenging but creates scenic landscapes

blocks.content: Betlingchip (939 m above sea level) in the Jampui Hills of North Tripura is the highest point in Tripura. The Jampui Hills stretch along the boundary between Tripura and Mizoram. The hill range is famous for its cool climate, orange orchards, and scenic beauty — earning it the nickname 'Switzerland of Tripura.' The Orange Festival is held here annually.
